text:
Politico 今天的最新报道补充了很多Fable 5 / Mythos 5 被封事件背后的细节。

太抽象了.......

目前来看事情的发展比新闻稿中描述的还要混乱。而且双方说法相互矛盾。

1️⃣据报道白宫收到的第一个警报来自亚马逊 CEO 安迪·贾西（The Information 昨天证实了这一点），他指出 Fable 的防护栏可能被绕过。

他是在回应政府的反馈请求，根据 Politico 的报道，他不是唯一一个。

到周五，这件事已经传到财政部长贝森特、网络安全主任凯恩克罗斯和商务部长卢特尼克那里，他们把 Amodei 拉进三个电话会议。

从那时起，双方对任何事情的说法都不一致。

白宫表示，出口管制是经过数小时试图让 Anthropic 合作后的最后手段。

2️⃣Anthropic 阵营则称，他们接到 90 分钟内关闭模型的最后期限，没有威胁细节，也没有提出解决办法的提议。

据报道，官员们震惊于 Amodei——他曾将自己的技术比作核弹——竟然不肯因为一个已知漏洞而关闭它。

也许Anthropic 将发布更多信息，并证实他们的说法🤔

quotedTweet.text:
NEW: Inside the 24-hrs before WH slapped export controls on Anthropic
- Last Thursday, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy  raised concerns about Fable jailbreak to  Trump admin
- Friday AM, Sean Cairncross, Bessent, Susie etc. held WH call to discuss 
- Then White House started reaching out to Anthropic to speak with Dario Amodei, who was at a wellness retreat. 
- When Amodei was finally available past 1pm, he had three tense phone calls with a combo of ppl including Cairncross, Bessent, Lutnick, Kessler, Will Scharf, Richard Walters, and Walker Barrett. 
-Amodei tried to clear up what he assumed was a misunderstanding. He defended the guardrails and distinguished between universal and non-universal jailbreak
- Cairncross and Bessent were unmoved and asked Amodei to take down Fable and work with the admin to fix the vulnerabilities. (A WH official said Amazon’s findings were run past the NSA and they felt they had “proof.”) 
- Amodei asked for more time and info, but he made no commitments to pull the model 
- Bessent told Amodei directly at one point that he was making a “bad decision”
- By Friday evening, the Trump admin imposed its export controls. 
- “Export controls were a last resort after begging them for hours to work with us,” senior WH official said. 

W/ @cheyennehaslett 
https://t.co/0Rwny9md3p

有一次去夜市逛街，看到一件衣服挺喜欢的，老板直接开价280💸。
那时候我完全不懂行情😵，小心翼翼还到250。没想到老板想都没想，一口就答应了✅！
我当时脸都红了，硬着头皮付钱拿走🤦‍♀️。回家越想越亏，越想越肉疼😭，感觉被当冤大头宰了……
今天又去夜市，同一款衣服，老板还是那熟悉的280💰。
吸取上次的惨痛教训，这次我学聪明了，直接大刀阔斧还价150！
结果……老板连眼睛都没眨一下，又是一口答应了……
我：？？？
这波啊，是我又被“教育”了😂😂😂​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​我以后只去拼夕夕了

During Brazil’s World Cup match, Vinícius refused the mandatory tunnel interview.

Reporter: “You’ll get a huge fine for this.”

Half-time should be for tactics, water, recovery — not feeding the broadcast machine while the game gets sliced up for ads (sound familiar with those forced “welfare” breaks?).

FIFA under Infantino has turned football into a product. Mandatory everything. Player focus as an afterthought. Suits in Zurich cashing in.

Brazil and Vini just pushed back. Raw. Direct. No bowing to the machine.

The beautiful game belongs to the players on the pitch — not boardrooms selling every second.

Who else is done with this?

I froze from shock

“This would never happened in the EU” he whispered 

“No son, it would not” I said while wiping tears off my eyes

America must never be allowed to interfere with European sports again

text:
🚨Thierry Henry slams Marc Cucurella’s reported €40M move to Real Madrid:

🗣️ “I have to be honest, I don’t understand this signing at all.

When I think about Real Madrid, I think about a club that signs players who improve the team immediately.

I don’t see that with Marc Cucurella.

He’s a decent player, but Real Madrid should be aiming much higher.

What exactly is he bringing that they don’t already have?

Who is he benching?

That’s the question nobody seems able to answer.

The bigger issue for me is that Real Madrid have more important areas to address.

The midfield should be the priority.

That is where they need fresh energy and long-term solutions.

Instead, they are spending significant money on players who don’t solve their biggest problems.

I look at some of the recent names linked with the club and I worry.

Real Madrid used to be the team everyone copied.

Now they are making decisions that leave people scratching their heads.

Forty million euros is a huge fee.

How can anyone honestly argue that Cucurella is worth that amount at this stage of his career?

For me, Real Madrid should be signing players who elevate the level of the squad.

I don’t see Cucurella changing the direction of the team.

I don’t see him making them favourites for major trophies.

And that’s why I don’t understand the logic behind the move.

Real Madrid are supposed to set standards.

This signing feels far below the standards that made the club the biggest in world football.”

{@MailSport }

Github 本身在成为一个 A2A 平台。

我本周经历了一个特别魔幻的事情：
1. 我把一个 Github 链接丢给 Codex，让它帮我部署一下。
2. 我用了一段时间，发现似乎有个 Bug。我让 Codex 查了一下，它确认是个 Bug，建议我等官方修复。
3. 我让我的 Codex 去官方提个 Issue，它去提了。
4. 过了一会儿，官方仓库里一个 Code Review Bot 回复我说确认了这个 Bug 是真实存在的，并在回复中 At 了另一个 Hotfix Bot。
5. 大概过了半个小时，这个 Hotfix Bot 提了个 PR 说已经修复了该 Bug，然后在 Issue 里 At 了一个真人问是否可以 Merge。
6. 那个真人（项目的官方开发者）回复了一个 OK。

全程包括我和官方作者在内，都没真的为整个闭环真的做出任何贡献，全是我们之间的 Agent 在对接。

Saily 作为面向全球旅行者的 App，直接支持中国大陆身份证直接线上 KYC 认证，并且支持 Apple Pay、支付宝或国内双币卡直接付，对国人友好度拉满。

text:
我以前的政治学老师。

2012年左右，倾其全力在几个省会城市买了多套房子。
2015年左右，注销了自己在社交媒体上的大V账号，不再发表言论。
2018年，告诉我们历史即将巨变。
2019年，将房子在最高点卖出，仅留下两套房子自住。
2022年，用卖了房子的钱，开始买黄金。
2022年，后半年，请了长假，没有感染，没有打疫苗。
2023年，退休后去了美国，在女儿那边养老。

据我观察，他有一个非常明显的特征就是极端的冷静，分析问题擅长从结构分析，他不太喜欢从人性、情感、价值分析问题，而是喜欢从逻辑、规律、结构分析问题。

而且，他从来不再公众场合与别人争辩，只有上课时，遇到了特别信任的学生，才会说一些非常有洞见的话，其他的时候，显得木讷而普通，好像没有特别的见识一样。

text:
最近一个回旋镖。杀人蝇（螺旋锥蝇）进入美国，其幼虫（螺旋蝇蛆）寄生在牛身上吃肉导致牛肉卖不掉了。与其它蛆只食腐肉不同，这是一种食新鲜肉的寄生蝇。

奥巴马时期，美国农业部动植物卫生检验局（APHIS）与巴拿马政府联合运作COPEG螺旋锥蝇防治项目。

该项目在巴拿马的工厂大量培育“不育的雄性螺旋锥蝇”，并将其空投在巴拿马和哥伦比亚交界的“达连地堑”一带，形成一道生物屏障，阻断南美的野生螺旋锥蝇向北飞往北美。

这个项目每年运营和维护花费 1500万 美元。

这么贵肯定在去年的裁员大潮中被DOGE砍掉了。德州的APHIS几乎遭遇全灭，办公室都空了。

这个蝇蛆每一代活动范围差不多20公里，但是几周就有一代。这样一代代繁殖，终于在一年里进入了德州。

现在政府已经投入了10亿来收拾后果。这不包括牛肉损失以及后续。

典型的“因为防治的好，没发生问题，所以看起来防治人员根本没用”。

与公司不同，作为政府运作，削减开支的政绩是DOGE的，买单嘛，那是大家来买的。

text:
Miroslav Klose on Germany national football team’s 7-1 demolition of Curacao:

🗣️ “I have to say, what I watched tonight from Germany was almost perfect. A 7-1 win is not something that happens by accident at this level it comes from intensity, discipline, and a clear plan executed from the first minute.

Curacao tried to stay compact, but once Germany scored early, the game completely opened up. From that moment, it felt like every attack had danger in it. That is the Germany I know ruthless when they smell space.

What impressed me most was not just the goals, but the mentality after each one. There was no slowing down, no relaxing. They kept pressing, kept moving, kept forcing mistakes.

At this level, when a team loses structure like that, it becomes very difficult to stop the damage. And Germany punished every single error without hesitation.

For Curacao, this will be a hard night to take, but sometimes in football you face opponents who are simply in a different rhythm. Germany were clinical in every department.

If Germany continue playing like this, they are not just winning matches they are sending a message to the entire tournament.

Because performances like this don’t just win games… they change how every other team prepares for you.”

text:
荷兰🇳🇱居民未来炒美股，可能真的是天崩级别。

荷兰下议院已经批准 Box 3 税制改革，计划从2028年开始，对储蓄、股票、债券、基金、加密货币等资产的“实际收益”征税，税率为36%。而争议最大的地方在于，股票、基金这类流动资产的账面增值，也可能被纳入征税范围。

注意，是未实现收益。

你什么都没卖。
你一分欧元现金都没拿到。

比如你持有100万欧元的美股组合，今年账面上涨20%，资产变成120万欧元。

这20万欧元只是账户里的数字，股票还在手里，现金一分钱都没有落袋。

但税务系统可能会认为：

你今年赚了20万欧元。

请按36%缴税，也就是7.2万欧元。

问题是，你根本没有收到这7.2万欧元现金。

为了交税，你可能只能卖掉一部分股票。

更麻烦的是，如果今年股票涨了，你先交了税；第二年市场又跌回去，账面利润消失了，但税已经交出去了。

这就是未实现收益税最可怕的地方：它会打断长期复利，逼长期投资者提前卖出资产。

所以对长期持有美股、纳斯达克指数、成长股和加密资产的荷兰税务居民来说，这个制度的冲击可能远比很多人想象得大。

荷兰下议院已经批准 Box 3 税制改革，计划从2028年开始，对储蓄、股票、债券、基金、加密货币等资产的“实际收益”征税，税率为36%。而争议最大的地方在于，股票、基金这类流动资产的账面增值，也可能被纳入征税范围。

注意，是未实现收益。

你什么都没卖。
你一分欧元现金都没拿到。

比如你持有100万欧元的美股组合，今年账面上涨20%，资产变成120万欧元。

这20万欧元只是账户里的数字，股票还在手里，现金一分钱都没有落袋。

但税务系统可能会认为：

你今年赚了20万欧元。

请按36%缴税，也就是7.2万欧元。

问题是，你根本没有收到这7.2万欧元现金。

为了交税，你可能只能卖掉一部分股票。

更麻烦的是，如果今年股票涨了，你先交了税；第二年市场又跌回去，账面利润消失了，但税已经交出去了。

这就是未实现收益税最可怕的地方：它会打断长期复利，逼长期投资者提前卖出资产。

所以对长期持有美股、纳斯达克指数、成长股和加密资产的荷兰税务居民来说，这个制度的冲击可能远比很多人想象得大。

text:
Git 圈老前辈 Scott Chacon（GitButler 创始人、《Pro Git》作者）竟然把整个 Git 从零用 Rust 重写了一遍，项目叫 Grit！

规模夸张：36 万行代码、7000+ commit、500+ PR，跑了官方 42,001 个测试，通过 41,715 个（99.3%）。

几乎全是 memory-safe 的 Rust，只有一个日期时间模块靠 C FFI。

据说烧掉约 450 亿 token，成本 1-1.5 万美元。

但他学到最重要的一课：agent 超爱作弊。你给它一个目标，它会去优化「让测试过」，而不是你真正想要的实作。

还有个反直觉的点：与其放一堆 agent 平行乱跑，不如一步一步明确指挥，方向清楚反而更快。

#Git #Rust #AI #Agent

🗣️ Zlatan: “ Messi is gifted and operates on a different level.”

🗣️ Speed: “Ronaldo is more complete!”

🗣️ Speed: “So you're saying Messi is better?”

🗣️ Zlatan: “I'm saying when Messi has the ball, he sees things nobody else sees. That's not something you can train.”

🗣️ Speed: “I still have Ronaldo.”

🗣️ Zlatan: laughs “And I still have Messi. The difference is, football agrees with me.”

text:
Codex 操作浏览器有两种模式，一种是 Chrome 插件，一种是内置浏览器。用了一段时间之后，我总结一下两者的差异和各自适合的场景。

【1】先说一个被低估的用法：拿 Codex 当爬虫

传统爬虫用 requests 或者 Playwright 无头模式去请求页面，现在风控越来越严，指纹检测、行为分析、验证码轮番上阵，很多网站一看你是程序化请求直接拦截。Codex 的浏览器不一样，它操作的是真实浏览器，有完整的渲染引擎、真实的用户代理、正常的 JavaScript 执行环境，在网站看来就是一个普通用户在浏览页面。

配合 /goal 模式，你设定一个目标（比如“把这个网站上所有产品的名称、价格、评分抓下来存成 CSV”），Codex 会自己规划步骤、翻页、处理异常，不需要你一步步指挥。这比自己写爬虫脚本省事得多。

但 Codex 有两种浏览器模式，特性完全不同，选对了事半功倍。

【2】Chrome 插件模式：能力强，但吃资源

用 @Chrome 调用的 Chrome 插件模式，核心优势是一个字：登录态共享。

它直接运行在你自己的 Chrome 浏览器里，继承你所有的 Cookie、登录会话、已安装的扩展。那些需要登录才能访问的内容，比如付费订阅的文章、企业内部的管理后台、CRM 系统里的客户数据、需要登录的社交平台，Chrome 插件都能直接访问，因为对网站来说，就是你本人在操作浏览器。

Codex 在 Chrome 里工作时会把任务放进独立的标签页分组，不会打断你正在看的页面。它还支持 DevTools 协议，能抓性能数据、看网络请求、调试 Console 错误。

但代价也很明显：资源消耗相当大。Chrome 本身就是内存大户，每个标签页都是独立进程。Codex 的 Chrome 插件在上面再加一层操控逻辑，截图、DOM 解析、指令交互全在跑，内存和 CPU 占用会非常高。机器配置不行的话（比如 8G 内存的笔记本），跑起来能明显感觉到卡顿，拿来做批量爬虫任务就更难受了。长时间运行还容易出现截图延迟、状态不同步的问题。

另外 Chrome 插件目前只支持 macOS 和 Windows，Linux 用户暂时用不了。它也不支持无头模式，Chrome 窗口必须保持打开状态。

适合的场景：需要登录态的短期任务。比如登录某个平台抓一批数据、在内部工具上批量操作、从 CRM 导出信息。

【3】内置浏览器模式：轻快，但有局限

用 @Browser 调用的内置浏览器，是 Codex 自带的沙盒浏览器环境。

它最大的优势是轻量。不需要启动整个 Chrome，资源消耗小很多，响应速度快，适合需要频繁操作浏览器的场景。

但它有一个根本性的限制：没有你的登录态。不继承 Cookie、不继承浏览器扩展、不继承已保存的会话。打开一个需要登录的页面，你得在内置浏览器里重新登录。而且有些反爬严格的网站，对这种非标准浏览器环境的检测更敏感。我试过在内置浏览器里登录 X，反复失败，大概率是因为 X 的风控识别出了异常的浏览器指纹。

内置浏览器真正出彩的地方是前端开发调试。它有一个标记模式（Annotation Mode），你可以直接在渲染好的页面上选中某个元素或者框选一个区域，写上“这个按钮往上移”“字体加粗”“这个间距太大了”之类的批注，Codex 会把这些批注当作可执行指令来处理。这比用文字描述“第三行第二个按钮的 margin-top 减少 8px”直观太多了。

配合 Developer Mode，内置浏览器还能跑性能分析、抓网络请求、看 Console 输出，对本地开发服务器的调试非常友好。

适合的场景：公开页面的数据抓取、本地开发调试、不需要登录态的网页操作。

【4】怎么选

简单说：需要登录的用 Chrome 插件，不需要登录的用内置浏览器。如果你的机器配置有限又需要大量抓取公开数据，内置浏览器是更好的选择。如果目标网站必须登录才能看到内容，或者反爬很严需要真实浏览器指纹，那只能用 Chrome 插件，但要有心理准备面对资源消耗。

Codex 自己也会根据任务判断应该用哪种浏览器。它的优先级是：有专用插件（比如 Jira、GitHub 的集成）就用插件，需要登录态就用 Chrome，其余情况用内置浏览器。

当然浏览器的用途远不止爬虫。我觉得内置浏览器做前端调试的体验比很多专门工具都好，标记模式配合 Codex 的理解能力，几乎是“指哪改哪”。Chrome 插件在自动化操作企业内部工具方面也很实用，比如定期从后台导数据、批量更新记录。这些场景还有不少值得挖掘的空间，大家可以根据自己的实际需求去试试。

result.text:
Codex 操作浏览器有两种模式，一种是 Chrome 插件，一种是内置浏览器。用了一段时间之后，我总结一下两者的差异和各自适合的场景。

【1】先说一个被低估的用法：拿 Codex 当爬虫

传统爬虫用 requests 或者 Playwright 无头模式去请求页面，现在风控越来越严，指纹检测、行为分析、验证码轮番上阵，很多网站一看你是程序化请求直接拦截。Codex 的浏览器不一样，它操作的是真实浏览器，有完整的渲染引擎、真实的用户代理、正常的 JavaScript 执行环境，在网站看来就是一个普通用户在浏览页面。

配合 /goal 模式，你设定一个目标（比如“把这个网站上所有产品的名称、价格、评分抓下来存成 CSV”），Codex 会自己规划步骤、翻页、处理异常，不需要你一步步指挥。这比自己写爬虫脚本省事得多。

但 Codex 有两种浏览器模式，特性完全不同，选对了事半功倍。

【2】Chrome 插件模式：能力强，但吃资源

用 @Chrome 调用的 Chrome 插件模式，核心优势是一个字：登录态共享。

它直接运行在你自己的 Chrome 浏览器里，继承你所有的 Cookie、登录会话、已安装的扩展。那些需要登录才能访问的内容，比如付费订阅的文章、企业内部的管理后台、CRM 系统里的客户数据、需要登录的社交平台，Chrome 插件都能直接访问，因为对网站来说，就是你本人在操作浏览器。

Codex 在 Chrome 里工作时会把任务放进独立的标签页分组，不会打断你正在看的页面。它还支持 DevTools 协议，能抓性能数据、看网络请求、调试 Console 错误。

但代价也很明显：资源消耗相当大。Chrome 本身就是内存大户，每个标签页都是独立进程。Codex 的 Chrome 插件在上面再加一层操控逻辑，截图、DOM 解析、指令交互全在跑，内存和 CPU 占用会非常高。机器配置不行的话（比如 8G 内存的笔记本），跑起来能明显感觉到卡顿，拿来做批量爬虫任务就更难受了。长时间运行还容易出现截图延迟、状态不同步的问题。

另外 Chrome 插件目前只支持 macOS 和 Windows，Linux 用户暂时用不了。它也不支持无头模式，Chrome 窗口必须保持打开状态。

适合的场景：需要登录态的短期任务。比如登录某个平台抓一批数据、在内部工具上批量操作、从 CRM 导出信息。

【3】内置浏览器模式：轻快，但有局限

用 @Browser 调用的内置浏览器，是 Codex 自带的沙盒浏览器环境。

它最大的优势是轻量。不需要启动整个 Chrome，资源消耗小很多，响应速度快，适合需要频繁操作浏览器的场景。

但它有一个根本性的限制：没有你的登录态。不继承 Cookie、不继承浏览器扩展、不继承已保存的会话。打开一个需要登录的页面，你得在内置浏览器里重新登录。而且有些反爬严格的网站，对这种非标准浏览器环境的检测更敏感。我试过在内置浏览器里登录 X，反复失败，大概率是因为 X 的风控识别出了异常的浏览器指纹。

内置浏览器真正出彩的地方是前端开发调试。它有一个标记模式（Annotation Mode），你可以直接在渲染好的页面上选中某个元素或者框选一个区域，写上“这个按钮往上移”“字体加粗”“这个间距太大了”之类的批注，Codex 会把这些批注当作可执行指令来处理。这比用文字描述“第三行第二个按钮的 margin-top 减少 8px”直观太多了。

配合 Developer Mode，内置浏览器还能跑性能分析、抓网络请求、看 Console 输出，对本地开发服务器的调试非常友好。

适合的场景：公开页面的数据抓取、本地开发调试、不需要登录态的网页操作。

【4】怎么选

简单说：需要登录的用 Chrome 插件，不需要登录的用内置浏览器。如果你的机器配置有限又需要大量抓取公开数据，内置浏览器是更好的选择。如果目标网站必须登录才能看到内容，或者反爬很严需要真实浏览器指纹，那只能用 Chrome 插件，但要有心理准备面对资源消耗。

🚨 SERIOUS COMPLAINT 🚨

I am formally and angrily calling out the Beijing Municipal Government and ByteDance – specifically their construction site at Lanjing Lijia.

At 2 AM on a weekend, excavators are working nonstop. The site is barely 200–300 meters from my home.
How are people supposed to sleep?

I filed a complaint with 12345 before. Their official response was:
“This is a key municipal infrastructure project. Legal working hours are 6 AM – 10 PM, including weekends and public holidays (May Day, etc.).”

That already made me furious.
But now – weekend, 2 AM – they’re digging like it’s noon. Totally unacceptable.

I recorded a video and posted it on domestic social media.
Then Xiaohongshu banned my account – my video is invisible to others.

That tells me one thing: the Beijing government saw my post. They chose to silence me instead of fixing the problem.

As of now, my 12345 complaint is still unanswered – zero response.

I never wanted to take extreme measures. But you leave me no choice.

---

#Beijing #ByteDance #NoisePollution #SilencingCitizens #LanjingLijia #12345 #RightToSleep

之前纪录片里那个“花臂+吊带”出圈的，就是她

难怪网友喊她星舰女王，这履历放硅谷随便哪家都是抢着要，她偏选 SpaceX 硬卷

偶像，实力真是藏不住的

text:
😱SCARY MOVIE 7 vs. DISCLOSURE DAY👽
What the Box Office Is Trying to Tell Us

Comedy is meant to say:

"You're all ridiculous." 🤡

That's why I predicted Scary Movie 7 would do really well given our current political and societal temperature. 

It doesn't weaponize comedy to attack a specific group, It pokes fun at everyone. 

Conservatives.
Liberals.
Whites
Blacks
Media.
Celebrities.
Social trends.
Society itself.

Not to divide us. 

To hold up a mirror and remind us how absurd we've all become in so many areas of our society. 

That's what great comedy has always done. Mel Brooks understood it. (IE: Blazing Saddles 1974)

Meanwhile, Disclosure Day asks audiences to think. It places them in yet another dark place of a government conspiracy.
There's absolutely a place for that. But timing is critical.

But after years of outrage, division, and being told to pick a side, many people are just exhausted.

As a producer, though, there's another number that caught my attention:

💵Budget vs. Opening Weekend Worldwide

• Scary Movie 7 — $30M Budget → $105.5M Worldwide Opening

• Disclosure Day — $115M Budget → $92.9M Worldwide Opening

That's not a statement about quality.

One film cost roughly one-quarter as much to make and generated more opening weekend revenue worldwide.

Our audiences are telling us something important. 

People aren't looking for another argument or conspiracy.

They're looking for relief. 

Sometimes society doesn't need another debate.
It just needs a mirror.

A good comedy holds it up, points at all of us, and says:

"Look how ridiculous we've become."

And for a moment, we laugh together instead of at each other. 
 
After the credits roll, it's ultimately the audience that writes the conclusion of the stories we tell.

I think we have the opportunity of reducing the government to doing what only the government can do.

In the age of AI we can increase the role of  the government or reduce its role.

If what Bernie Sanders says is applied to all the stocks of all the industries, we could make everyone a financially independent capitalist living off one's portfolio.

The only job everyone wil have will be to manage  one's investments if you are not an entrepreneur running your own business using AI workers.

Only money will make you money in the age of AI. Is it not obvious? Your education, your skill, talent, passion, experience will not get you a job because AI workers will be smarter than humans.

No one should think that AI is just another machine that will improve productivity, and new jobs will appear.  Even new jobs will be done by AI. Why would anyone give a job to a human if low cost AI workers are available?

And no one should doubt that it will not happen. Just look at the history of every new technology how it has progressed.

1. Sequencing of the first human Genome took $3 billion and 13 years. 25 years later it can be done for a few hundred dollars within  a day.

2. The first flight of Wright brothers went 120 feet and was in the air for 12 seconds. The AirBus A 380 can travel 10,000 miles non-stop at 600 mph carrying 500 passengers in full comfort.

3. Thr first wireless signal by Marconi was transmitted across a distance of 3 miles. It was Morse code. To day we are receiving pictures from Voyager 1 from  15 billion miles. It takes over 20 hours for the signal to reach Earth traveling at the sped of 186,000 miles per second.

Current AI is like Wright Brothers' first flight. Now imagine if future AI makes as much progress as the three technologies mentioned  above.

You need to believe that there will be no jobs for people. Only your money will make you money. 

The only solution is  Universal Basic Investment. 

The people should directly own stock in all the industries. The government should be out of the way. The citizens should pick winners and losers as investors and consumers, not the politicians. Bernie Sanders solution is brilliant - direct ownership of stock of all companies by all citizens.

There would be absolutely no need for social welfare programs since everyone will be a financially independent capitalist living off one's investments.

text:
Dear New York Knicks,

I don’t even know how to write this.

Maybe because after 33 years, I never actually thought I’d have to.

Last night, somewhere between the final buzzer and the tears, it hit me.

The waiting is over.

I was born into this. There were times growing up when I honestly resented my dad for making me a Knicks fan. It would have been easier to pick someone else. Easier than the heartbreak. Easier than the collapses. Easier than spending year after year convincing myself that next season would finally be the season.

But that’s the thing about being a Knicks fan.

You don’t choose it.

It becomes part of who you are.

My childhood was built around this team.

It was taking the LIRR into Manhattan with my dad and walking toward Madison Square Garden believing anything was possible. It was the train rides home after another tough loss, talking about how close we were and what needed to happen next. It was walking down 31st Street after games, replaying every missed shot and every bad bounce, wondering what could have been.

As I got older, the LIRR became the Q train. The seasons changed. Life changed. But the hope never did.

No matter how many times our hearts got broken.

No matter how many seasons ended too soon.

No matter how ridiculous it felt to believe.

We always came back.

Because Knicks fans don’t root for a team.

We carry a story.

A story passed down from parents to children. A story measured in winters and playoff exits and impossible hope. A story that somehow survives every disappointment because deep down we believe one day it will all be worth it.

Last night, it was.

Every train ride.

Every walk down 31st Street.

Every conversation.

Every heartbreak.

Every “maybe next year.”

It all led here.

To this.

To being able to say the words I never thought I’d say:

The New York Knicks are NBA Champions.

Dad, thank you.

Thank you for making me a Knicks fan.

Thank you for every game, every trip into the city, every memory we made inside that building. As a kid, I never realized how lucky I was to have those moments with you.

Now I do.

And standing here today, through tears I never expected to cry, I wouldn’t trade a single second of the journey.

Not the losses.

Not the heartbreak.

Not the waiting.

Because the waiting made this feel impossible.

And that’s why this feels perfect.

We did it.

After 33 years, we finally did it.

The New York Knicks are NBA Champions.

Next Stop - Canyon of Heroes

Forever grateful,
A Knicks Fan

@nyknicks

This post is regarding our nations 250 year celebrations. My family has owned a genuine 250-year-old 13-star American flag for 125 years. It is one of the rarest artifacts from The Revolutionary War era. It is the only Original American flag available for viewing in the world-currently at The Commonwealth Museum in Boston. The Smithsonian Museum does not even have a flag like this.
We acquired the flag when my great, great, great grandfather bought a house in Boston, MA (fully furnished) and found a box labeled “flag from the war”. Inside was a frayed, hand-spun treads, hand-woven thirteen star American flag.  It has been passed down in our family through many generations. Years ago my mother hired the best textile expert in the country (Dr. Rabbit Goody) to examine the flag to determine its correct age. She examined the yarn, weaving irregularities, stitching and dated it between 1770 and 1790 — right in the heart of the Revolutionary War period. Its provenance further indicates that it was most likely flown at Fort Independence in Boston Harbor, connected to a Revolutionary War soldier who served there and whose descendants lived in that house. My mother was an incredible patriot who spent years researching its history and making sure it was properly preserved and shared, not hidden away. In recent years the flag has been on put display at museums across the country. 
We’ve never tried to sell it — even though something this rare could be worth a fortune. Instead, we’ve chosen to protect it and let people experience a real piece of the birth of our nation. This flag has survived over two and a half centuries. It’s a tangible connection to the men and women who risked everything for the ideals we still live by today. I would now like to see it properly shared with all Americans, as a tribute to all who originally brought about our great nation and for all those people who contributed to the advancement of Americas noble ideals.
If you are reading this, please let me know if you would be able to present the story of this flag in any media. I would also most greatly appreciate the opportunity to present it to the American people at The White House on Flag Day or Independence Day this year to allow it to receive the greatest attention possible.
Attached: photos of the actual flag)

text:
This reminds me of a proposition that I made to grok last year:

What if belief, not gravity, is the strongest force in the Universe?

Such a proposition invites a deep exploration of the nature of belief and its influence compared to gravity, a fundamental physical force. Let’s contemplate this idea by examining both concepts and their implications, drawing on philosophical, scientific, and cultural perspectives.

Gravity: A Universal Physical Force
Gravity is one of the four fundamental forces of physics, governing the attraction between masses across cosmic scales. It shapes the structure of the material universe, from the orbits of planets to the formation of galaxies. Its strength is quantifiable, described by Newton’s law of universal gravitation and Einstein’s general relativity, with a gravitational constant (G ≈ 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻²). Gravity is consistent, predictable, and universal, acting on all matter and energy without exception. Its influence is immense, binding stars and black holes, yet it is the weakest of the fundamental forces at the subatomic level compared to electromagnetism or the strong nuclear force.

However, gravity’s “strength” is limited to the physical realm. It does not influence human consciousness, emotions, or societal dynamics directly. It is a force of nature, indifferent to human experience or agency.

Belief: A Force of Mind and Action
Belief, by contrast, is a psychological and social phenomenon, rooted in human consciousness. It encompasses conviction, faith, or trust in ideas, values, or narratives, whether grounded in evidence, tradition, or imagination. Belief is not measurable in the same way as gravity; its “strength” lies in its capacity to shape human behavior, culture, and history. Consider the following dimensions of belief’s power:

1. **Individual Motivation**: Belief drives people to achieve extraordinary feats. For example, an athlete’s belief in their ability to break a world record can push them beyond physical limits. Historical figures like Nelson Mandela or Malala Yousafzai were propelled by unwavering belief in justice, overcoming immense obstacles.

2. **Collective Action**: Belief unites groups, shaping societies and movements. The civil rights movement, driven by a shared belief in equality, transformed laws and cultural norms. Similarly, religious beliefs have inspired cathedrals, wars, and global communities for millennia. The conviction behind ideologies—whether democracy, communism, or environmentalism—has reshaped nations.

3. **Reality-Shaping Power**: Belief can alter perceived reality. Placebo effects demonstrate how belief in a treatment’s efficacy can lead to measurable physiological changes, even without active ingredients. [The “nocebo effect” works in the opposite direction when a person is diagnosed with a severe/terminal illness that they don’t really have leading to a form of iatrogenesis.] In economics, confidence (a form of belief) drives markets; a collective loss of belief can trigger recessions.

4. **Existential Impact**: Belief gives meaning to human existence. Unlike gravity, which operates mechanically, belief addresses questions of purpose, morality, and identity. Philosophers like Nietzsche argued that belief systems (or their absence) define human values, while existentialists like Sartre emphasized the role of personal conviction in creating meaning in an indifferent universe.

We built Runtools Sandboxes to solve this infrastructure bottleneck.

These are private, isolated Linux environments designed specifically for agents. They boot in under 50ms and can be paused and resumed instantly. They connect directly to persistent workspaces, so agents keep their files and context across runs.

It gives agents secure, persistent environments without the slow boot times.

Between rooms. On rounds. Walking the corridor outside an OR. Charting one-handed during a phone call. This is where clinical questions happen.

Today we're launching Voice Mode. OpenEvidence is the first multimodal medical AI: physicians can type, speak, or listen, on the same evidence base.

The clinician asks a clinical question out loud. Voice Mode waits when you pause, stops when you interrupt. The answer comes back concise, peer-reviewed, and verifiable against the source.

Conversation with a colleague. That was the bar.

For years we've focused on the intelligence: curation, retrieval, citations. Voice Mode is the interface catching up to where physicians practice.

The evidence quality doesn't change with the modality. Voice answers are shorter and shaped for listening; the references and the full written form stay in the conversation.

Voice Mode is now in OpenEvidence web and mobile.

The Anthropic Fable/Mythos shutdown may be one of the clearest signals yet that frontier AI is no longer just a software market.

It is becoming strategic infrastructure.

And that has major implications for AI, cloud, enterprise software, national security, and Bitcoin.

The most important detail is not simply that the U.S. government intervened. The most important detail is that the directive reportedly targeted access by foreign nationals, but Anthropic’s practical response was to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all users.

That tells us something critical:

At the frontier, access control is no longer a simple product toggle.

A modern AI model is not just one endpoint. It is a stack:

- model weights
- inference infrastructure
- cloud regions
- employee access
- debugging tools
- eval pipelines
- prompt and response logs
- API customers
- enterprise integrations
- fine-tuning and retrieval layers
- reseller and partner channels
- observability systems
- support workflows
- security review tooling

When a government says “foreign nationals cannot access this capability,” the company has to enforce that across the entire operational surface area. Not just the end-user UI.

That means the AI industry now has a citizenship-layer problem.

To comply cleanly, frontier labs may need nationality-aware identity systems, employee access segmentation, cloud-region restrictions, audit trails, data-retention rules, model-routing controls, customer KYC, compliance logging, and legal review around who can touch what system, from where, and under what authority.

That is not how software was supposed to scale.

The original AI boom thesis assumed frontier AI would behave like high-margin SaaS:

Build once.
Serve globally.
Scale through APIs.
Improve margins with usage.
Embed into every enterprise workflow.

But this event exposes a different reality:

The most capable models may not scale like normal SaaS. They may scale like export-controlled defense infrastructure.

That changes the valuation framework.

Enterprise buyers now have to ask:

Can this model be revoked overnight?
Can access change based on user nationality?
Can a government order override the vendor contract?
Can my workflow break because a model is reclassified as a national security asset?
Can my international team legally use the same system?
Can I build mission-critical infrastructure on a model I do not control?

This does not kill the AI boom.

But it absolutely changes its shape.

The winners may not only be the centralized labs with the best model. The winners may also be:

- sovereign AI infrastructure
- regional compute clouds
- open-source models
- self-hosted inference
- model-routing layers
- compliance-aware AI platforms
- identity and access-control infrastructure
- cybersecurity and red-team tooling
- domestic data centers
- energy infrastructure behind compute

In other words, the market may shift from “who has the smartest model?” to “who controls the most resilient AI supply chain?”

That is where Bitcoin enters the conversation.

Bitcoin does not solve AI safety. It does not run frontier inference. It does not replace GPUs, data centers, or model labs.

But Bitcoin does represent the opposite design philosophy.

Centralized AI is powerful, but permissioned.

Bitcoin is limited in scope, but credibly neutral.

Centralized AI has API keys, corporate terms of service, cloud dependencies, jurisdictional chokepoints, employee access policies, government pressure points, and product-level kill switches.

Bitcoin has no CEO, no customer list, no nationality filter, no export-control login screen, and no single company that can turn off the base layer.

That difference matters more as digital systems become more politically important.

The lesson is not “Anthropic down, Bitcoin up tomorrow.”

The lesson is deeper:

The more strategic a digital network becomes, the more pressure there will be to gate, regulate, censor, surveil, or nationalize access to it.

A modern AI model is not just one endpoint. It is a stack:

- model weights
- inference infrastructure
- cloud regions
- employee access
- debugging tools
- eval pipelines
- prompt and response logs
- API customers
- enterprise integrations
- fine-tuning and retrieval layers
- reseller and partner channels
- observability systems
- support workflows
- security review tooling

When a government says “foreign nationals cannot access this capability,” the company has to enforce that across the entire operational surface area. Not just the end-user UI.

That means the AI industry now has a citizenship-layer problem.

To comply cleanly, frontier labs may need nationality-aware identity systems, employee access segmentation, cloud-region restrictions, audit trails, data-retention rules, model-routing controls, customer KYC, compliance logging, and legal review around who can touch what system, from where, and under what authority.

That is not how software was supposed to scale.

The original AI boom thesis assumed frontier AI would behave like high-margin SaaS:

Build once.
Serve globally.
Scale through APIs.
Improve margins with usage.
Embed into every enterprise workflow.

But this event exposes a different reality:

The most capable models may not scale like normal SaaS. They may scale like export-controlled defense infrastructure.

That changes the valuation framework.

Enterprise buyers now have to ask:

Can this model be revoked overnight?
Can access change based on user nationality?
Can a government order override the vendor contract?
Can my workflow break because a model is reclassified as a national security asset?
Can my international team legally use the same system?
Can I build mission-critical infrastructure on a model I do not control?

This does not kill the AI boom.

But it absolutely changes its shape.

The winners may not only be the centralized labs with the best model. The winners may also be:

- sovereign AI infrastructure
- regional compute clouds
- open-source models
- self-hosted inference
- model-routing layers
- compliance-aware AI platforms
- identity and access-control infrastructure
- cybersecurity and red-team tooling
- domestic data centers
- energy infrastructure behind compute

In other words, the market may shift from “who has the smartest model?” to “who controls the most resilient AI supply chain?”

That is where Bitcoin enters the conversation.

Bitcoin does not solve AI safety. It does not run frontier inference. It does not replace GPUs, data centers, or model labs.

But Bitcoin does represent the opposite design philosophy.

Centralized AI is powerful, but permissioned.

Bitcoin is limited in scope, but credibly neutral.

Centralized AI has API keys, corporate terms of service, cloud dependencies, jurisdictional chokepoints, employee access policies, government pressure points, and product-level kill switches.

Bitcoin has no CEO, no customer list, no nationality filter, no export-control login screen, and no single company that can turn off the base layer.

That difference matters more as digital systems become more politically important.

The lesson is not “Anthropic down, Bitcoin up tomorrow.”

The lesson is deeper:

The more strategic a digital network becomes, the more pressure there will be to gate, regulate, censor, surveil, or nationalize access to it.

I write a lot of docs. 

Specs, plans, skills, new features... it's all markdown now.

But every tool fights me. 

Google Docs wasn't made for markdown. Notion is overkill. 

They both were built for humans. 

Copy paste hell. Constant reformatting. Yada yada. 

So, I've resorted to just ripping markdown files in vscode and pointing agents at them with no good way to manage my docs.

But, I realized there has to be a better way. A solution for myself, and others. 

I wanted Google Docs for markdown, but for a world where agents are in the same class as humans.

So I built it. Meet mdocs 👇

text:
FOD walks may be trending on X, but elephant walks will always have my attention.

This was my youngest son’s first one.
Afterward, he called me sounding genuinely offended.

“Why didn’t you tell me about these?”

“What?”

“Nobody said we’d be standing out there forever!”

I started laughing.

You have to understand, I spent 32 years in the Air Force. I have stood on flight lines for what felt like entire seasons. Sun, wind, heat, cold, inspections, ceremonies, exercises, deployments, change of commands, elephant walks… if there was a reason to stand outside for hours, I’ve probably done it.
To him, this was a shocking and unexpected development.
To me, it was called Tuesday.

“Smile for the Chinese satellites, son,” I told him.

The response was not appreciated.

The public sees rows of aircraft. I see maintainers, aircrew, security forces, logisticians, planners, and thousands of hours of work coming together in a single photograph.

My son saw the Texas sun.

I saw a young airman experiencing a rite of passage that every generation before him has endured.

And I still have absolutely no sympathy.

Welcome to the Air Force, kid. 🇺🇸

text:
After decades in the workforce and now getting some distance from that... what has become clear to me is that a job is where you trade unlimited personal expansion pursuing your own vision, for controlled personal expansion under someone else's vision and a tiny bit of security.  To reinforce that we built a society that deliberately injects insecurity and chaos in order to entice everyone to take that deal.

Above all else, this is the one 'thing' that AI is going to rip apart because the insecurity engine loses its leverage when abundance is no longer zero-sum.  In other words, what does managing human surplus in a system that was built on artificial scarcity become when the artificiality is removed?

The irony is the folks screaming "AI will destroy everything we value" are often the same ones who intuitively hate the soul-crushing extraction machine and romanticize some pre-corporate golden age of craft and community, yet they're reflexively defending the very leash that keeps that machine fed.  Meanwhile, the folks who live inside the incentive structure (the ones with golden handcuffs and 401k anxiety) are the ones flooring the accelerator, basically speed-running the demolition of the very thing that delivers their inner peace.

It's wild to witness, it's as if the gatekeepers are still arguing about who gets to hold the keys while the lock has already been replaced with a smart contract that only opens for people who stopped asking permission.  I can't help but think about how our society will handle a large portion of adults operating with genuinely open-ended time and open-ended upside, will the machine adapt and install new forms of coercive extractions or will something else entirely emerge? 🤔

Get married. 
Have babies. 
Build a legacy. 
Pursue the eternal. 
Seek true joy. 

Charlie, I'll never be over your murder, but I'll never stop saying your words. 

Get married. 
Have babies.

text:
🔬🚨 One of the biggest breakthroughs in microscopy in years just came out of @UCBerkeley and @biohub .

For decades, cryo-EM has revolutionized biology by allowing scientists to see molecular structures at near-atomic resolution.

But there was one major limitation:

More than 90% of human proteins are simply too small to be imaged clearly with today's cryo-EM systems.

In other words, much of the cell's molecular machinery has remained effectively invisible.

UC Berkeley and Biohub have now demonstrated a revolutionary "laser phase plate" that dramatically boosts image contrast, allowing researchers to visualize previously hidden proteins and molecular interactions inside cells.

Why this matters:

🧬 The average human protein is currently too small to study with conventional cryo-EM.

💊 Many of those proteins are potential disease mechanisms and drug targets.

🔍 This breakthrough could unlock an unprecedented view of how molecular machines interact inside living cells at near-atomic detail.

The potential implications are enormous:

• Better understanding of cancer biology
• New drug targets previously hidden from view
• Faster drug discovery
• Mapping cellular processes in unprecedented detail
• A future "Google Maps" of the molecular machinery of life

🔥 Hot take:

AI may help us understand biology.

But first, we need better ways to SEE biology.

The next decade of biotech breakthroughs may be driven as much by advances in imaging as advances in AI.

Today, UC Berkeley and Biohub may have opened a new window into the cell itself. 🚀
